violations.why: req1 sets irq=0 and later checks irq==0. Higher-priority req6 (or req3, req5, req7 or req8) can preempt in between and set irq=-1, so the check sees a different value.
req6 writes irq=-1 and then tests it. Higher-priority req7 or req8 can preempt and write irq=0, so the test fails.
req3 sets global_id=-1 in exit and then tests it. A higher-priority ISR such as req5 can run init and overwrite it in between.
JudgeCondi runs in req1 and reads var1 twice. Higher-priority req3 can write var1 between the two reads.
JudgeCondi in req1 reads var2 twice. req3 can preempt between the reads and write var2.
req7 writes array[9000] and later reads it. Higher-priority req8 can preempt in between and overwrite it with 999.
